uncited: *   **Input:** A 3D scalar field (volume data), a transfer function mapping scalars to color and opacity, and a set of parallel polygons (typically quads) representing the view-aligned slices.
*   **3D Texture:** A 3D texture object with dimensions matching the volume data resolution.
*   **Polygon Set:** A collection of parallel quads.
**Texture Population:** Map the scalar values from the input volume data into the 3D texture.
For each voxel at position $(i, j, k)$ with scalar value $s$, compute the color $C$ and opacity $\alpha$ using the transfer function $T(s) = (R, G, B, \alpha)$.
**Coordinate Definition:** Define texture coordinates for the parallel polygons.
The coordinates are linearly mapped to the 3D texture space.
**Geometry Setup:** Place the set of parallel polygons into a display list.
Render the parallel polygons in back-to-front order (or front-to-back with appropriate blending setup) through the 3D texture.
The cost is dominated by texture interpolation and framebuffer compositing.
The approach leverages early OpenGL capabilities for 3D texture mapping and display lists to achieve real-time performance.
